question: What is the default vertical alignment of texts in an Excel worksheet?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bottom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

In Microsoft Excel, when you enter text or numbers into a cell, the software applies default alignments for both horizontal and vertical axes. While the horizontal alignment varies (text to the left, numbers to the right), the vertical alignment is set to the Bottom for all types of data by default.

**Detailed Breakdown of Alignment**

To better understand how Excel handles your data, here are the default settings:

__
 
• Vertical Alignment: Always Bottom. This means the text "sits" at the base of the cell.
 
• Horizontal Alignment (Text): Left.
 
• Horizontal Alignment (Numbers): Right. This helps when aligning decimal points in a column of figures.

**Changing the Alignment**

You can modify these settings by navigating to the Home tab and looking in the Alignment group. The vertical options include:

 
• Top Align: Aligns text to the top edge.
 
• Middle Align: Centers text between the top and bottom edges.
 
• Bottom Align: The default setting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **A group of cells arranged in rows and columns** is referred to as a worksheet in **Excel documents.**
 
• It is the work surface that you use to input data.
 
• Each worksheet functions as a massive table for organizing data with** 1048576 rows and 16384 columns.**
 
• A workbook typically has numerous worksheets with connected content, but only one of them is open at any given moment.
